name: MonarchTimesheetGrid
title: TimesheetGrid
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.PrimaryScrollableTabRow and Tab with MonarchDurationInput per row (one day at a time); androidx.compose.foundation.text.BasicTextField with androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextFieldDefaults.DecorationBox, androidx.compose.foundation.horizontalScroll and CollectionInfo semantics (the grid); androidx.compose.material3.TextButton (cells that open entries); androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu (row actions); android.icu.text.DateFormat
summary: A period of time entry, usually a week: rows of projects or tasks against days, with typed durations, row, day and period totals, locked days and a daily limit.
whenToUse: For weekly time entry and review in time-tracking, payroll and project apps, where people log time per project per day and see the totals as they type. Save each change in onCellChange and pass the new rows.
whenNotToUse: Not for a single duration; use MonarchDurationInput. Not for live tracking; use MonarchRunningTimer. Not for what changed between versions of a timesheet; use MonarchTimesheetDiff. Not for general tabular data; use MonarchDataTable.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchTimesheetGrid(days: List<MonarchTimesheetGridDay>, rows: List<MonarchTimesheetGridRow>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, summaryRows: List<MonarchTimesheetGridSummaryRow> = emptyList(), maximumMinutesPerDay: Int = 1440, layout: MonarchTimesheetGridLayout = MonarchTimesheetGridLayout.Automatic, readOnly: Boolean = false, emptyMessage: String? = null, labels: MonarchTimesheetGridLabels = MonarchTimesheetGridLabels(), actionsIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, rowActions: ((MonarchTimesheetGridRow) -> List<MonarchDataTableRowAction>)? = null, onDayActivate: ((day: Long) -> Unit)? = null, onCellActivate: ((rowId: String, day: Long) -> Unit)? = null, onCellChange: (suspend (rowId: String, day: Long, minutes: Int) -> Unit)? = null)

class MonarchTimesheetGridDay(date: Long, label: String? = null, today: Boolean = false, nonWorking: Boolean = false, locked: Boolean = false, lockReason: String? = null, note: String? = null, expectedMinutes: Int? = null)
class MonarchTimesheetGridRow(id: String, label: String, description: String? = null, cells: Map<Long, Int> = emptyMap(), readOnly: Boolean = false) { fun minutes(on: Long): Int }
class MonarchTimesheetGridSummaryRow(id: String, label: String, cells: Map<Long, String> = emptyMap(), total: String? = null) { fun text(on: Long): String? }
enum class MonarchTimesheetGridLayout { Automatic, Grid, Day }

class MonarchTimesheetGridLabels(caption: String? = null, rowHeader: String? = null, total: String? = null, dayTotal: String? = null, days: String? = null, rowActions: ((row: String) -> String)? = null, actionsText: String? = null, cellLabel: ((row: String, day: String) -> String)? = null, locked: String? = null, noTime: String? = null, invalid: String? = null, tooLong: ((maximum: String) -> String)? = null, saveFailed: String? = null, expected: ((duration: String) -> String)? = null, overLimit: String? = null, empty: String? = null, today: String? = null, saving: String? = null, periodTotal: ((duration: String) -> String)? = null, duration: ((minutes: Int) -> String)? = null, spokenDuration: ((minutes: Int) -> String)? = null, shortDay: ((day: Long) -> String)? = null, longDay: ((day: Long) -> String)? = null)

options.name: days
options.description: The days in order, usually a week. A day can be today, non-working, locked (with a reason), carry a note and an expected number of minutes. Its date is a day key: any time on that date in UTC, as epoch milliseconds.

options.name: rows
options.description: The rows with their minutes per day, keyed by day key. A read-only row never takes typing.

options.name: summaryRows
options.description: Display-only footer rows with text per day, such as attendance.

options.name: maximumMinutesPerDay
options.description: The largest value a cell accepts, and the day total above which a day is flagged.

options.name: layout
options.description: Automatic shows the grid when every column fits and the font scale is at most 1.3, otherwise one day at a time; Grid or Day forces one.

options.name: readOnly
options.description: Makes every cell read-only, for example after submission. Wins over onCellChange.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: Shown when there are no rows (or no days). Built in: "No time logged for this period."

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, the duration formats and the day formats.

options.name: actionsIcon
options.description: The icon of each row's actions button. Without it the button shows the text "Actions".

options.name: rowActions
options.description: The actions of a row, in a menu beside its name, such as clearing the row. The same type MonarchDataTable uses.

options.name: onDayActivate
options.description: Makes day headings buttons, for example to open a day view.

options.name: onCellActivate
options.description: Makes read-only cells with time buttons, for example to open the entries behind them.

options.name: onCellChange
options.type: (suspend (rowId: String, day: Long, minutes: Int) -> Unit)?
options.description: Saves a typed value: row id, day key and minutes (0 clears). The cell is disabled and read as "Saving" while it runs; a thrown exception's message is shown. Without it, every cell is read-only.

states.name: editable
states.description: Open cells are outlined fields in the grid, or MonarchDurationInput fields in the day layout; the text is read when focus leaves or on the Next key (the Done key in the day layout), and the minutes are passed to onCellChange.

states.name: saving
states.description: The cell is disabled, its text uses the disabled color and it is read as "Saving" (in the day layout its helper text says "Saving") until onCellChange returns.

states.name: error
states.description: Text that cannot be read, a value above the daily maximum or a failed save keeps the typed text, gives the cell the danger border and error semantics, and shows the message under the grid in a polite live region (in the day layout, under the field).

states.name: locked day
states.description: The heading shows the reason, or "Locked"; the column is shaded and its cells are muted, read-only and read with the reason.

states.name: read-only row or grid
states.description: Cells show the time as text, a dash when empty. With onCellActivate, cells with time are Material 3 text buttons in the link color.

states.name: today
states.description: The heading says "Today" in the strong accent color, with an accent bar under it in the grid; the day layout opens on it.

states.name: non-working day
states.description: The column (or the day heading) is shaded; entry is still allowed.

states.name: over the daily limit
states.description: The day total is in the strong danger color with the words "Over limit" under it.

states.name: empty
states.description: Without rows the empty message replaces the rows; without days the day layout shows only the message.

appearance: Headings and the first column use the label style; the header and footer rows use the subtle background, with the muted text color for column headings, descriptions, notes, expected times and summary rows. Locked and non-working columns use the subtle background; today's heading uses the strong accent color with a bar in the solid accent; errors and over-limit totals use the strong danger color with words. Fields use the input border on the surface and the focus ring color when focused, like MonarchTextField. All roles come from the theme, so dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web always renders a table that scrolls sideways; on a phone that is hard to use, so the automatic layout shows one day at a time with a Material 3 PrimaryScrollableTabRow of the days, a MonarchDurationInput (with its − and + steppers) for each editable row and the row's period total under it, as iOS does with its day pages. iOS moves between days with previous and next buttons; Android uses tabs, the Material 3 pattern, so it has no previousDay and nextDay labels. The web keys days and cells by ISO date strings and iOS by Date; here the key is a day key, epoch milliseconds in UTC as in the Material 3 DatePickerState (minSdk 24, no java.time), and any time on the same UTC day matches. The web returns a promise and iOS an async throwing closure from onCellChange; here it is a suspend function, and a thrown exception's message is shown. The web's label, markers and summary cells accept any content; here they are text. The web's row actions slot takes any content; here row actions are MonarchDataTableRowAction values in a Material 3 DropdownMenu beside the row name, with an optional actionsIcon slot because Monarch bundles no icons. The web moves between cells with all four arrow keys; here, with a hardware keyboard, Enter (the Next key) saves and moves down, up and down arrows move between rows, Escape restores the saved value and left and right move the text cursor. The over-limit total says "Over limit" in words where iOS shows a symbol. Locked days have no lock glyph, only the reason or "Locked" in words.
accessibility: The grid is a collection named "Time per row and day" (labels.caption) with its row and column counts; each cell carries its row and column.
Column headings, row names and day headings are headings; a day heading is one element read in full, such as "Mon, Jan 12, Approved" or "Tue, Jan 13, Today".
Each cell is named by its row and day, such as "Atlas, Tue, Jan 13"; a read-only cell's state is the time in words and the lock reason, such as "4 hours, Approved", or "No time" when empty.
An editable grid cell is a text field with that name; it carries error semantics with the message while rejected, and the state "Saving" while it is saved.
Error messages appear under the grid in a polite live region, so TalkBack announces them, and are words, not only the danger color.
Day totals are named "Day total, <day>" and read the time in words, the expected time and "Over limit"; row totals are named "<row>, Total".
In the day layout the day tabs are Material 3 tabs in a row named "Days", each read in full and marked selected; the page opens on today.
Day headings with onDayActivate, cells with onCellActivate and the row actions button are buttons with a 48dp touch target.
Above font scale 1.3 the automatic layout shows one day at a time so no text is cut; long names wrap.
edgeCases: Negative minutes in cells count as 0; two keys on the same UTC day are added together.
Cells keyed by a day that is not in days are ignored in every total.
Empty text clears the cell: onCellChange receives 0.
A value equal to the saved one is not passed to onCellChange.
If onCellChange succeeds but the app does not pass new rows, the typed text stays in the cell until the row's value changes.
A lockReason locks the day even when locked is false.
readOnly wins over onCellChange; without onCellChange every cell is read-only.
The day layout opens on today, else the first day, and stays where the person moved it.
The grid does not scroll vertically: place it in a scrolling screen. It scrolls sideways when the columns do not fit.

examples.template:
@OptIn(ExperimentalMonarchApi::class)
MonarchTimesheetGrid(
    days = listOf(
        MonarchTimesheetGridDay(date = {{days.0.date|millis}}, expectedMinutes = {{days.0.expectedMinutes}}),
            MonarchTimesheetGridDay(date = {{days.1.date|millis}}, today = {{days.1.today}}, expectedMinutes = {{days.1.expectedMinutes}}),
            MonarchTimesheetGridDay(date = {{days.2.date|millis}}, expectedMinutes = {{days.2.expectedMinutes}}),
            MonarchTimesheetGridDay(date = {{days.3.date|millis}}, locked = true, lockReason = {{days.3.locked}}, expectedMinutes = {{days.3.expectedMinutes}}),
            MonarchTimesheetGridDay(date = {{days.4.date|millis}}, expectedMinutes = {{days.4.expectedMinutes}}),
            MonarchTimesheetGridDay(date = {{days.5.date|millis}}, nonWorking = {{days.5.nonWorking}}),
            MonarchTimesheetGridDay(date = {{days.6.date|millis}}, nonWorking = {{days.6.nonWorking}}),
    ),
    rows = listOf(
        MonarchTimesheetGridRow(id = {{rows.0.id}}, label = {{rows.0.label}}, description = {{rows.0.description}}, cells = cells[{{rows.0.id}}] ?: emptyMap()),
        MonarchTimesheetGridRow(id = {{rows.1.id}}, label = {{rows.1.label}}, description = {{rows.1.description}}, cells = cells[{{rows.1.id}}] ?: emptyMap()),
        MonarchTimesheetGridRow(id = {{rows.2.id}}, label = {{rows.2.label}}, description = {{rows.2.description}}, cells = cells[{{rows.2.id}}] ?: emptyMap()),
        MonarchTimesheetGridRow(id = {{rows.3.id}}, label = {{rows.3.label}}, description = {{rows.3.description}}, cells = cells[{{rows.3.id}}] ?: emptyMap(), readOnly = {{rows.3.readOnly}}),
    ),
    summaryRows = listOf(
        MonarchTimesheetGridSummaryRow(id = {{summary.id}}, label = {{summary.label}}, cells = mapOf({{summary.cells.0.date|millis}} to {{summary.cells.0.text}}, {{summary.cells.1.date|millis}} to {{summary.cells.1.text}}, {{summary.cells.2.date|millis}} to {{summary.cells.2.text}}), total = {{summary.total}}),
    ),
    rowActions = { row ->
        if (row.readOnly) emptyList() else listOf(MonarchDataTableRowAction(title = {{rowAction}}, onClick = { cells = cells + (row.id to emptyMap()) }))
    },
    layout = MonarchTimesheetGridLayout.Grid,
    onCellChange = { rowId, date, minutes ->
        cells = cells + (rowId to (if (minutes == 0) (cells[rowId] ?: emptyMap()) - date else (cells[rowId] ?: emptyMap()) + (date to minutes)))
    },
)

MonarchTimesheetGrid(
    days = listOf(MonarchTimesheetGridDay(monday, today = true, expectedMinutes = 480)),
    rows = listOf(MonarchTimesheetGridRow("atlas", "Atlas", cells = mapOf(monday to 450))),

parityExceptions.reason: The web shows a row's actions menu only while the pointer is over the row or a control in it has focus, so its still image has none. A touch screen has no hover, so each editable row keeps a visible three dots button (a 48dp touch target) that opens the same Clear row menu.
parityExceptions.convention: no hover on touch: a control that appears on hover on the web is always visible on a phone (Material touch target of 48dp)
